clue.text: Strip with sex appeal for gangster

blocks.note: a band is a narrow strip of material
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A gangster who strips off and has plenty of sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed robber or outlaw, near enough a synonym for a violent criminal mobster.

clue.text: Ostracise a cricketer

blocks.note: first meaning: shun or refuse to deal with
second meaning: Geoffrey ..., the Yorkshire and England batsman

explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England opening batsman, later a commentator.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott is to refuse dealings with someone as a protest, and the surname belongs to a well-known England batsman.

clue.text: Promote and organise endless unrest

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new order
without an end, so the last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A call to stir up and organise unrest that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse an idea or project is to foster and encourage it, helping it grow.

clue.text: Flash Labour leader may end being on the spot

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter counts
the end is the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: in a flash means in an instant

explanation.surface: A Labour Party leader might suddenly find their career ending on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: On the spot is an idiom meaning immediately, without any delay at all.

clue.text: Is dead duck in quarantine?

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of the others, so the duck sits inside

blocks.note: the late king means the dead king
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Asks whether a dead duck has been put into quarantine, as with bird flu.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, written as the letter that looks like nought.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine is to keep a person or animal apart from others to stop disease spreading; isolate is the verb synonym.

clue.text: Ken will smash pot found in desk

indicators.note: smashing breaks things to pieces that are put back differently

explanation.surface: Ken is going to break a pot he found in his desk.
explanation.walkthrough: Old school desks had a hole holding a small ink pot.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkwell is a small container for ink, once set into a hole in a school desk.

clue.text: Overdose on some valium? Shame!

indicators.note: some means only part, so a portion of the drug name is kept and the rest dropped

blocks.note: the tranquilliser, of which only the tail is kept

explanation.surface: Someone overdoses on tranquillisers and is met with disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is the disgrace or hatred attached to someone because of their conduct, close to opprobrium.

clue.text: All extremely overweight men get, initially, tiny ration

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends
initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Every very fat man is put on a tiny food ration.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a share allocated to someone, so a portion or allowance.

clue.text: Covered in unguent, I certainly tantalise!

indicators.note: the letters lie wrapped inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone smeared in ointment boasts of being seductive.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to tempt or lure, much as tantalising draws someone on with something desirable.

clue.text: "Echo" was a Maxwell paper once

blocks.note: first meaning: to copy or reflect back
second meaning: the Daily ... tabloid, owned by Robert Maxwell

explanation.walkthrough: Echo is also a newspaper title, but here it is a verb. Robert Maxwell owned the Daily Mirror, a British tabloid, until 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror is to reflect or copy closely, and the Daily Mirror tabloid was once in Robert Maxwell's media empire.

clue.text: Police HQ's taking credit for measure

blocks.note: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, often just 'the Yard'; plus the 's
buying on tick is buying on credit

explanation.surface: Police headquarters claims credit as a measure of its success.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police; 'on tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used for judging things, so a measure in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Holm has a tenant

blocks.note: a house that has a tenant is let; 'has' is read as the verb part
a property with a tenant is said to be let

explanation.surface: Reports that a property called Holm has a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has a tenant' becomes 'is let', which runs together as one word. Holm looks like a house name or surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A holm is a small island, especially in a river, the same thing as a little island in other wording.

clue.text: Operation time for Norma?

blocks.note: OP is the short form of operation; that the whole run also sits at the front of this word is a coincidence
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Asks when a woman called Norma is due for her operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma is not a patient but Bellini's opera, so the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a famous bel canto work by Bellini, an instance of staged musical drama.

clue.text: Doctor, I hurt: came with swollen joints

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A patient tells the doctor they are in pain and arrived with swollen joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like someone being addressed, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatism causes painful inflamed joints, so someone rheumatic suffers from swelling and stiffness there.

clue.text: Gutless tergiversator, a single Tory, almost becomes turncoat

indicators.note: removing the guts leaves only the outside of the long word
almost means not quite all, so the party word loses its end

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spineless Tory who keeps changing sides ends up as a defector.
explanation.walkthrough: A tergiversator is someone who changes sides, which fits the surface neatly. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is a person who deserts their side for the enemy, which is what a betrayer does.

clue.text: Revolutionary's terribly rash antic

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's stunt is described as dreadfully reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist seeks to overthrow government entirely, so a radical rebel or revolutionary.

clue.text: Gee, perhaps it's in the post

blocks.note: first meaning: gee is how the seventh character of the alphabet is spelt out
second meaning: a written message sent by mail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gee' reads as an exclamation of surprise, but it is the name of the alphabet character G.
explanation.definitionFit: G is one character of the alphabet, and a written note sent through the mail is also called by this word.

clue.text: Time to act: ICI takes on an expert planner

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Chemical giant ICI decides to act and hires a strategist.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a big British company.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician is skilled at planning moves and manoeuvres to achieve an aim.

clue.text: Ravine in Tuscany, once hidden

indicators.note: the clue says outright that something is concealed inside the neighbouring words

explanation.surface: A ravine in Tuscany that was once hidden from view.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge, so it is a larger relative of a narrow steep-sided valley.

clue.text: Sewers are not entirely unnecessary

indicators.note: not the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A claim that drains are not wholly superfluous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains, but it means things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as 'things that sew', sewers are the pointed tools used to pull thread through cloth.

clue.text: Concert I enter by the back passage

indicators.note: the letter goes into the phrase that follows, as a person enters a room

blocks.note: rectal means by way of the rectum

explanation.surface: A concert-goer slips in through the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The innocent-looking back entrance is really the anatomical one: I goes inside RECTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, often by one soloist, so a kind of concert.

clue.text: Thinking highly of sailor

blocks.note: first meaning: valuing or esteeming someone
second meaning: a non-commissioned seaman in the navy

explanation.walkthrough: A rating is an ordinary seaman, not an officer, in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is to hold them in esteem, and a naval rating is an enlisted seaman.

clue.text: Lynne, it's said, catches birds

indicators.note: said points to how the name and words are pronounced

blocks.note: the name and contraction run together

explanation.surface: A woman named Lynne is said to catch birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Linnets are small brown finches known for their song, so they are songbirds.

clue.text: Flee first east then south to South African province

blocks.note: the Cape Province of South Africa

explanation.surface: Directions for running away: head east, then south, to South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to get away from danger or captivity, which is what fleeing does.

clue.text: California city curtailed religious ceremony

indicators.note: curtailed literally means having its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: A Californian city cuts back its religious ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a Christian rite such as baptism or communion, held as a channel of divine grace.

clue.text: Department in pursuit of a skilled person

explanation.surface: A department is hunting for a skilled recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In pursuit of' tells you DEPT comes after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is an expert, someone highly proficient at something.

clue.text: Old Peruvian's in jail

blocks.note: the can is American slang for prison

explanation.surface: An ancient Peruvian has ended up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest, so an ancient Peruvian native is an Incan.

clue.text: Unrefined and ignorant support for Conservative

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
rude in its old sense of uneducated, unlearned

explanation.surface: Mocks a coarse, ill-informed supporter of the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a support sits below what it holds up, so RUDE goes under C.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is unrefined, and crude manners are coarse, so the adjective means not processed or polished.

clue.text: A&E's admitting 54: quick!

indicators.note: a hospital admits patients, taking them inside, so the number goes within

blocks.note: the two letters of the hospital department name

explanation.surface: The casualty department admits patient number 54 and urges haste.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (accident and emergency) is the British hospital casualty department. 'Quick' is the old sense, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its archaic sense means living, as in the biblical phrase about judging the living and the dead.

clue.text: Train line dug to line east -- or west -- of Greenwich

definitions.text: line east -- or west -- of Greenwich

indicators.note: to train something is to shape or discipline it into a new form

explanation.surface: A railway line has been dug out to run east or west from Greenwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train line' looks like a railway, but Train is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Longitude measures position east or west of the prime meridian, which passes through Greenwich in London.

clue.text: Lands in east Massachusetts and Maine, for instance

explanation.surface: Describes landholdings in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates are large areas of land owned by one person or family, so properties or lands.

clue.text: Infuriates Her Majesty and 'angs about

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: hangs with the H dropped, as in Cockney speech

explanation.surface: The Queen is annoyed at someone who loiters around.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'angs shows a dropped H, so the word is taken without it.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to make them furious, a plain verb synonym for infuriates.
